description_preview:
Company Description
MAGMA Energy is a consulting company established in 2005, specializing in upstream petroleum engineering services across subsurface and surface operations for both onshore and offshore fields. The company brings together an expert, multidisciplinary team including geophysicists, reservoir engineers, drilling engineers, petrophysicists, geologists, production engineers, and upstream surface engineers. MAGMA Energy also provides process, mechanical, electrical, civil, instrumentation, and HSE services, supporting complex projects in the oil and gas industry. In addition to consulting, the company operates as a training provider, offering courses across all petroleum disciplines. Its structure includes several specialized sections, such as advisory, subsurface, upstream surface, exploration, training, drilling, and software development.
Role Description
The AI Software Engineer will design, develop, and deploy AI-driven software solutions that support MAGMA Energy’s petroleum engineering, exploration, and training activities. This full-time hybrid role is based in the Atlanta Metropolitan Area, with a mix of on-site collaboration and work-from-home flexibility. Day-to-day responsibilities include building and optimizing machine learning and neural network models, implementing pattern recognition algorithms, and applying natural language processing (NLP) techniques to domain-specific data and documentation. The engineer will contribute to end-to-end software development, from requirements gathering and architecture design through coding, testing, and deployment, ensuring solutions are reliable, scalable, and aligned with business needs. Collaboration with domain experts and cross-functional teams is expected to translate complex engineering challenges into AI-powered tools and services.
Qualifications
Strong foundation in Computer Science and Software Development, including algorithms, data structures, and modern programming languages (e.g., Python, C++, or Java).
Experience with Pattern Recognition and Neural Networks, including model design, training, evaluation, and optimization using common ML frameworks (e.g., TensorFlow, PyTorch).
Knowledge of Natural Language Processing (NLP), such as text classification, information extraction, and working with unstructured technical documents.
Familiarity with AI/ML lifecycle tools (version control, CI/CD, model deployment, and monitoring) and best practices for reproducible, maintainable code.
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science, or a related technical field; exposure to petroleum or energy industry data is a plus.
Ability to work effectively in a hybrid environment, communicate clearly with technical and non-technical stakeholders, and collaborate in multidisciplinary teams.
Experience with cloud platforms, data pipelines, or MLOps, and an interest in applying AI to engineering, geoscience, or industrial applications.

Electrical Engineer (New Grad December 2026)

ELECTRICAL ENGINEER (NEW GRAD DECEMBER 2026)
Freeform builds AI-native manufacturing systems that unify software, hardware, and physics to produce industrial-scale parts at the speed of human ideation. By treating manufacturing as a single integrated system, we unlock a new era of innovation where complex hardware is designed, built, and scaled without limits.
As an Electrical Engineer at Freeform, you will play an integral role in the design and development of custom electronics that bring our advanced metal 3D printing factory systems to life. You’ll work with a talented engineering team from some of the world’s most innovative companies on electrical system design, development, and integration efforts across the factory systems, with a specific focus on PCB and compute system design. You will use a first-principles approach to solving problems and tackling new areas within electrical engineering that you may not have directly worked on before. 3D printing experience is not required to be successful here - rather we look for smart, motivated, collaborative engineers who love solving hard problems and creating amazing technology!

Rapidly design, develop and test highly reliable electronics and PCBs

Job Description
We are seeking an entry-level Manufacturing Engineer to support continuous improvement initiatives within a fast-paced manufacturing environment. This role focuses on enhancing production efficiency, improving Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE), reducing downtime, and supporting process optimization efforts across multiple production lines. supports translational research in image-guided surgery and collaborates closely with data scientists, engineers, clinicians, and scientific partners to advance innovative approaches in surgical care.

Job Title: Plant Engineer
Job Description
The Plant Engineer supports day-to-day engineering, facilities, utilities, maintenance, and project activities across a food manufacturing plant. This hands-on role focuses on keeping projects moving, improving equipment reliability, supporting maintenance execution, and ensuring facility systems operate safely, compliantly, and efficiently. The Plant Engineer partners closely with Facilities, Maintenance, Engineering, Production, Quality, Safety, contractors, and vendors to support daily operations, capital projects, utility systems, preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, documentation, and continuous improvement. This position suits someone who enjoys being on the plant floor, solving technical problems, communicating effectively, and managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
Responsibilities
Support the Facilities Manager with daily facilities, utilities, maintenance, and project activities across the plant.
Take ownership of follow-ups, action items, quotes, schedules, contractor coordination, and project documentation to keep work moving forward.
Conduct daily floor walks to identify facility issues, utility concerns, safety items, project progress, and repair needs.
Follow up on open facility issues, repairs, work orders, and department requests to ensure timely resolution.
Help prioritize urgent needs versus planned work to balance reliability, safety, and productivity.
Verify that completed work meets expectations and adheres to Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) standards.
Communicate regularly with Production, Warehouse, Quality, and Maintenance teams on active issues and status updates.
Escalate risks, delays, or safety concerns quickly to the appropriate stakeholders.
Assist with planning, tracking, and executing facility and utility projects from scope development through completion.
Create clear scopes of work for contractors, vendors, and internal maintenance teams.
Request quotes, compare proposals, follow up with vendors, and help prepare purchase requisitions and project justifications.
Gather field information such as measurements, photos, equipment data, and drawings to support project planning.
Develop project scopes, contractor walk-through notes, and bid comparison summaries to support decision-making.
Coordinate schedules with vendors, contractors, production, and maintenance to minimize operational disruption.
Track materials, parts, lead times, permits, and installation requirements to keep projects on schedule.
Monitor project progress and help ensure work is completed safely, on time, and within scope.
Support shutdown planning, weekend work, equipment installations, and project tie-ins as needed.
Assist with layout changes, equipment moves, room build-outs, piping modifications, utility upgrades, and facility improvements.
Support troubleshooting and root cause analysis for facility and utility systems, including HVAC, boilers, air compressors, chillers, pumps, fans, process piping, water systems, wastewater systems, docks, doors, and building systems.
Contribute to reliability improvements for boilers, air compressors, HVAC, chillers, pumps, fans, water systems, and other facility equipment.
Review work orders, identify repeat failures, and help develop corrective actions to reduce downtime and recurring issues.
Help build critical spare parts lists and enhance preventive maintenance tasks to improve equipment reliability

Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related technical field preferred.
0–2 years of experience in manufacturing, facilities, utilities, maintenance, project engineering, or plant engineering preferred.
Strong mechanical and technical understanding of industrial facility systems.
Experience working with contractors, vendors, maintenance teams, and production teams.
Experience in food, beverage, packaging, or other regulated manufacturing environments preferred.
Experience with AutoCAD, basic layouts, P&IDs, or equipment drawings preferred

This is a Permanent position based out of Graham, NC.

Work for Indiana
Begin a fulfilling career with the State of Indiana by joining one of the largest employers in the state, offering a range of opportunities across 60+ agencies. At the state, you'll find competitive compensation, a robust benefits package and a commitment to work-life balance. Most importantly, you'll have the chance to make a real and measurable impact on the lives of Hoosiers across Indiana.
About The Indiana Department Of Transportation
The Indiana Department of Transportation (INDOT) provides a dynamic workplace that serves Indiana citizens, improves our state’s quality of life, and enhances its economic opportunity. INDOT has a number of innovative programs and projects, including Public-Private Partnerships, Green Initiatives, and cutting-edge uses of materials and assets. As part of the State of Indiana, INDOT offers a competitive total compensation package, as well as outstanding work/life balance. Whether you are an established professional in the transportation field or just starting your career, INDOT has exciting and challenging opportunities for you.
Role Overview
This position is responsible for developing comprehensive engineering designs for various transportation projects, ensuring successful execution by contractors and stakeholders. The construction projects may include roadway and bridge maintenance, temporary traffic control, signals, intersection improvement, drainage, right-of-way, and earthwork.
Engineer Trainee
A Professional Engineering license is not required for this position. Candidates who have an Engineering degree and a current Engineer in Training license (EIT), but do not hold a professional license, may be hired at a lower minimum salary and are eligible for promotional increases upon achieving milestones including years of experience and obtaining their Professional Engineering license. Upon obtaining a Professional Engineer license, the salary traditionally starts at an annual salary of $75,010 but may be commensurate with education or work experience.
Location:
This position is with INDOT's Greenfield District.
Salary
This position traditionally starts at an annual salary of $75,010.00 but may be commensurate with education and job experience. Use our
Compensation Calculator
to view the total compensation package.
A Day In The Life
The essential functions of this role are as follows:
Planning & Project Management: Serve as a resource for proposal development and research process. Ensure milestones, deliverables, and implementation strategies, are established accurately. Assist supervisor in the development of strategic planning and resource utilization.  You will participate in providing project reviews in accordance with the Agency’s established performance standards. Ensure that all plans reflect the scope of services, existing field conditions, appropriate design standards, and sound engineering judgment.
Program Management: Coordinate programs and plans for the division/department; interpret laws, regulations, and guidelines within area of assignment; review program plans for completeness, economic and technical feasibility.
Design and Research: Assist in the development of programs, research development & technology plans (road maps) to improve product quality. Review research proposals and report to ensure their accuracy, effectiveness, and potential for implementation.
Inspection: Organize, conduct, and review engineering investigations, field observations, which have a defined scope.
Technical & Data Analysis: Assist in analyzing engineering data and developing technical guidelines, technology initiatives, training course materials and other technical documents.
Testing: Assist in laboratory testing with “research grade equipment” related to materials/bridge/traffic research
Quality Control: Participate in Quality Control / Quality Assurance programs to ensure policy and best practices are actively deployed, analyze field data, and review plans for conformance to design criteria.

Investment Profile
Seed-stage infrastructure company in New York building an agentic development platform for the next generation of autonomous physical systems.
The company's AI-native platform helps engineering teams model, validate, test, and continuously improve complex real-world systems in software before deployment. Rather than replacing simulation engines, it orchestrates the engineering workflow surrounding simulation, validation, testing, and continuous improvement, dramatically shortening engineering feedback loops while reducing dependence on expensive real-world testing.
The founding team combines deep expertise across autonomy, AI, distributed systems, and enterprise software, and is assembling an exceptionally technical, in-person engineering team in New York City.
Summary
This isn't a traditional simulation engineering role.
It's about building the engineering platform that makes simulation useful.
You'll work across systems engineering, simulation, developer infrastructure, sensing, calibration, validation, performance, and customer engineering. Some weeks you'll build reusable platform capabilities. Others you'll work directly with customers to understand why reality doesn't quite match the model, then turn those learnings into engineering workflows that every future customer can benefit from.
The problems are rarely clean. You'll regularly encounter unfamiliar hardware, noisy sensor data, incomplete information, and ambiguous customer requirements. Success comes from reasoning from first principles, building robust software abstractions, and creating systems that engineers can trust.
If you enjoy difficult technical problems, high ownership, and building foundational infrastructure from scratch, this is one of the most interesting opportunities we've seen in Physical AI.
What You'll Build
Build reusable platform capabilities for modeling, calibration, validation, and continuous testing.
Transform messy real-world systems into accurate, production-quality digital representations.
Design engineering workflows that automate complex simulation, validation, and debugging tasks.
Improve simulation fidelity, determinism, correctness, scalability, and performance.
Build developer tooling that dramatically accelerates customer onboarding and engineering iteration.
Work directly with customers to understand unfamiliar systems, then generalize those learnings into reusable platform capabilities.
Help define the architecture and technical direction of an agentic development platform for autonomous physical systems.
You'll work closely with the founders and early engineering team across platform engineering, AI infrastructure, simulation, and customer deployments.
What We're Looking For
You likely have experience with several of the following:
Building robotics, autonomy, perception, simulation, computer vision, or other software systems that interact with the physical world.
Developing production software in Python (Rust or C++ is a plus).
Working with physical systems, sensing technologies, calibration, system identification, or quantitative validation.
Building developer platforms, infrastructure, or internal tooling used by other engineers.
Shipping production-quality engineering systems rather than research prototypes.
Operating effectively in ambiguous, fast-moving startup environments.
Experience with robotics simulation platforms, digital twins, physics engines, autonomy stacks, or related technologies is valuable, but we're ultimately looking for exceptional systems engineers who enjoy reasoning about real-world systems, learning unfamiliar domains, and building reusable engineering platforms.
Prior startup experience is a strong plus.
Our ideal candidate has high agency, cares deeply about engineering quality, enjoys working across disciplines, and wants to own difficult technical problems from first principles through production.
About Us
Greylock is an early-stage investor in hundreds of remarkable companies including Airbnb, LinkedIn, Dropbox, Workday, Cloudera, Facebook, Instagram, Roblox, Coinbase, Palo Alto Networks, and many others. Learn more at https://greylock.com/
How We Work
We are full-time, salaried employees of Greylock and provide free candidate referrals and introductions to our active investments. description_preview:
This is a job that Jill, our AI Recruiter, is recruiting for on behalf of one of our customers.
She will pick the best candidates from Jack's network.
The next step is to speak to Jack.
Job Title
Founding Engineer
Salary
£100k-£120k + Equity
Company Description
Iridium Credit is a London-based fintech, backed by a multi-million-dollar seed round from top US VCs and Entrepreneurs First, automating the $7 trillion US invoice financing market. Founded by veterans from Morgan Stanley and Microsoft, the company builds AI agents that verify invoices for bank-owned lenders processing $100M+ monthly.
Job Description
As the first founding engineer at Iridium Credit, you will build and own production AI agents across browser, voice, and email. Working directly with founders from Morgan Stanley and Microsoft, you'll solve complex verification challenges for bank-owned lenders, architecting reliable systems that process hundreds of millions in monthly invoice value for small businesses.
Location
London, UK
Why this role is remarkable
Work on a $7 trillion problem building "self-healing" AI agents and voice systems that navigate complex B2B dialpads and portals for bank-owned lenders.
Backed by a multi-million-dollar seed round from two major US VCs and Entrepreneurs First, with live contracts already processing $100M+ in monthly volume.
Transition with the company from London to New York in the coming months, with full US visa sponsorship and relocation costs covered by the company.
What You Will Do
Design and deploy sub-agent architectures that handle browser automation, CAPTCHAs, 2FA, and real-time voice interactions with accounts payable teams using Python.
Own features end-to-end as employee number four, making critical architectural decisions across the backend, frontend, and infrastructure to ensure bank-grade system reliability.
Collaborate directly with lenders and founders to understand commercial context and bridge the gap between technical builds and complex banking compliance requirements.
The ideal candidate
Strong engineering generalist with deep Python experience and a track record of building reliable systems that work against the messiness of the real-world web.
Experience with browser automation (Playwright/Puppeteer), AI agents, or production ML, particularly systems requiring high reliability when operating within changing external environments.
High-growth mindset with the appetite for early-stage startup intensity, ready to step into an engineering lead role within the next twelve months as the team expands.
Who are Jack & Jill?
Ok, I'll go first. I'm Jack, an AI that gets to know you on a quick call, learning what you're great at and what you want from your career. Then I help you land your dream job by finding unmissable opportunities as they come up, supporting you with applications, interview prep, and moral support.
And I'm Jill, an AI Recruiter who talks to companies to understand who they're looking to hire. Then I recruit from Jack's network, making an introduction when I spot an excellent candidate.
How does this work?
Jack's an AI agent for job searching and career coaching. He works for you.
Jill is the AI recruiter working for the company. She recruits from Jack's network.
If it's a match and the company wants to meet you, they'll make the intro. In the meantime, if you'd like, Jack will send you excellent alternatives.
We never post fake jobs
This isn't a trick. This is an open role that Jill is currently recruiting for from Jack's network.
Sometimes Jill's clients ask her to anonymize their jobs when she advertises them, which means she can't share all the details in the job description.
We appreciate this can make them look a bit suspect, but there isn't much we can do about it.
Give Jack a spin! You could land this role. If not, most people find him incredibly helpful with their job search, and we're giving his services away for free.
